Fast Prediction Intervals with a Global Residual Scale

Source: R/gam_fast_ci.R
gam_fast_ci.Rd

Fast prediction intervals from one monotone GAM fit and a single residual variance.

Computes prediction intervals of nearly constant width from a single monotone GAM fit. About four times faster than gam_adaptive_pi(), whose width follows the local scatter.

Usage

gam_fast_ci(rt_matrix, newdata, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

rt_matrix

A 2-column matrix [rt_source, rt_target].

newdata

Numeric vector of x-values for predictions.

alpha

Significance level (default 0.05 for 95% PI).

Value

A matrix with 3 columns: [predicted, lower, upper].

Details

Algorithm:

  1. Fit the monotone GAM (fit_gam_mono()).

  2. SE: pointwise standard errors of the unconstrained GAM.

  3. sigma^2: mean squared leave-one-out residual. The residuals of the constrained fit are divided by 1 - h, with h the leverages of the unconstrained GAM. In-sample residuals underestimate the error for new compounds, most of all with few compounds.

  4. Interval: prediction +/- z * sqrt(SE^2 + sigma^2), with bounds made non-decreasing by isotonic regression and the lower bound truncated at 0 (monotone_interval()).
